added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  If \(d\geq 2s_0\), then there are constants \(c>0\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\) and fixed bump shapes, such that
\[
 \rho_n^*\geq c\max\left\{
 n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},
 n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}
 \right\}
\]
for every \(n\geq n_0\).  The second term is certified by original fixed-\(n\) priors on the unchanged binary exact-uniform-design class: every component of the null prior has exactly \(\tau\equiv1/8\), and every component of the alternative prior has centered \(L^2(\lambda)\) separation bounded below by a constant multiple of \(n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\).  There is no logarithmic loss in this converse at \(d=2s_0\).  In particular, when \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\),
\[
 c n^{-2/7}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4/19},
 \qquad
 \frac{\rho_n^*}{\rho_{n,e}^*}\geq c n^{4/35}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
Put \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  We first construct the nuisance lower bound.  Fix the bounded-overlap tensor-product bump system used in \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection-corrected}\).  Such a system can be obtained by taking a nonnegative smooth function that is positive on a smaller cube, normalizing its integer translates to a locally finite squared partition of unity, and multiplying the fine functions in each macro cube by a smooth macro cutoff.  If the cutoff is denoted by \(g_Q\), then the resulting fine functions satisfy \(G_Q=\sum_{j\subset Q}B_j^2=g_Q^2\).  Local finiteness gives a fixed overlap constant, rescaling gives the synthesis inequalities in equation (1) of that lemma, and the region where one normalized translate is bounded below supplies the required fine-cell cores.  All constants in what follows may depend on this fixed system and on \(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,d,L\), but not on \(n\).

Fix a sufficiently small constant \(\epsilon>0\) and set
\[
 \delta_n=\epsilon n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)},
 \qquad
 q_e=2\delta_n^{\alpha/s_0},
 \qquad
 q_b=2\delta_n^{\beta/s_0}.
\]
Then \(q_eq_b=4\delta_n\), so the four-atom correlation parameter in equation (2) of the cited construction is
\[
 \vartheta=\frac{\delta_n}{q_eq_b}=\frac14.
\]
In particular all four atom probabilities are nonnegative.  Choose dyadic mesh widths \(h_n,H_n\) as follows.  For a fixed sufficiently large \(K_h\), take the smallest dyadic number satisfying
\[
 h_n\geq K_h\delta_n^{1/s_0}.
\]
For a fixed sufficiently large \(K_H\), take the smallest dyadic number satisfying
\[
 H_n\geq\max\{4h_n,K_H\delta_n^{1/\gamma}\}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), both widths are at most one, their reciprocals are integers, and \(H_n/h_n\) is an integer at least four.  Dyadic rounding changes either displayed scale by a factor smaller than two.  Hence
\[
 h_n\asymp\delta_n^{1/s_0},
 \qquad
 H_n\asymp\max\{h_n,\delta_n^{1/\gamma}\}.
\]

We verify every construction constraint.  The fine-scale Hölder quantities obey
\[
 C_bq_eh_n^{-\alpha}\leq2C_bK_h^{-\alpha},
 \qquad
 C_bq_bh_n^{-\beta}\leq2C_bK_h^{-\beta}.
\]
Choose \(K_h\) so that both right sides are at most \(L/2\).  Since \(H_n\geq4h_n\) and \(s_0-\beta=\alpha>0\),
\[
 2C_b\delta_nH_n^{-\beta}
 \leq 2C_b\delta_n(4h_n)^{-\beta}
 \leq C\delta_n^{1-\beta/s_0}
 =C\delta_n^{\alpha/s_0}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The CATE correction satisfies
\[
 4C_b\delta_nH_n^{-\gamma}\leq4C_bK_H^{-\gamma},
\]
which is at most \(L\) after increasing \(K_H\).  Finally \(q_e,q_b,\delta_n\to0\), so for all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 C_bq_e\leq\frac14,
 \qquad
 C_bq_b+2\delta_n\leq\frac18.
\]
These are precisely the smoothness and margin inequalities (5) of \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection-corrected}\).  That lemma therefore proves that every induced law belongs to \(\mathcal P(\alpha,\beta,\gamma,L,d)\), that every null component has \(\tau\equiv1/8\), and that every alternative component satisfies
\[
 c_D\delta_n\leq D(P_1)\leq C_D\delta_n
\]
for fixed positive constants \(c_D,C_D\).  Its construction also gives exact uniform design, consistency, conditional exchangeability, and the three pointwise interior boxes; these properties are thus componentwise, not merely properties of the prior predictives.

We next prove the fixed-sample comparison.  Condition on all macro signs \(\sigma=(\sigma_Q)\).  Under the null prior, the fine pairs are independent across fine coordinates and have the correlated four-atom law in equation (2) of the cited construction; under the alternative prior they are independent across fine coordinates and within each pair.  For nonnegative integers \(r,t\), direct summation over the four atoms gives
\[
 \mathbb E_0(U^rV^t\mid\sigma_Q)-\mathbb E_1(U^rV^t)
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \vartheta\sigma_Qq_e^rq_b^t
 =\delta_n\sigma_Qq_e^{r-1}q_b^{t-1},&r,t\text{ odd},\\
 0,&\text{otherwise}.
 \end{cases}
\]
Because \(q_e,q_b\leq1\) eventually, every nonzero moment discrepancy has absolute value at most \(\delta_n\).  The exact one-observation matching assertion of \(\texttt{lem:four-atom-cross-fine-third-projection-corrected}\) says that, conditional on \(\sigma\), the two one-observation prior-predictive laws coincide.

All Radon--Nikodym denominators are uniformly controlled.  Indeed, in every component and for every \(x\), the propensity and both arm regressions lie in \([1/4,3/4]\).  Thus each of the four conditional masses of \((A,Y)\) given \(X=x\) is at least
\[
 \min\{e(x),1-e(x)\}\min\{m_A(x),1-m_A(x)\}\geq\frac1{16}.
\]
The same lower bound holds after mixing.  Consequently every \(k\)-observation conditional binary mass used below is at least \(16^{-k}\).

Fix \(X_1=x_1,\ldots,X_n=x_n\).  Let \(N(i)\) be the set of fine-coordinate atoms whose bumps are nonzero at \(x_i\), and join sample indices \(i,j\) when \(N(i)\cap N(j)\neq\varnothing\).  Conditional on \(\sigma\), independence of the fine atoms makes each of the two predictive laws factor over the connected components of this graph.  A singleton component contributes no discrepancy because of exact one-observation matching.

Consider a connected component \(C\) of size \(k\geq2\).  Expand its conditional binary mass as a polynomial in its active \(U\)'s, \(V\)'s and the deterministic alternative corrections \(\delta_nG_Q\).  The displayed moment identity shows that a coefficient changed by the atom law contains a factor bounded by \(\delta_n\); a coefficient changed by the deterministic macro correction also contains such a factor.  All remaining amplitudes, scores, and bumps are bounded by one or by a fixed constant, and bounded overlap makes the number of monomials at most exponential in \(k\).  A telescoping expansion therefore yields, for every binary cell,
\[
 |r_{0,C}-r_{1,C}|\leq C_0^k\delta_n.
\]
Using the denominator bound and summing over the \(4^k\) binary cells gives
\[
 H^2(r_{0,C},r_{1,C})
 \leq\chi^2(r_{0,C},r_{1,C})
 \leq C_1^k\delta_n^2.
\]
For product distributions the Hellinger affinities multiply, so \(1-\prod_j a_j\leq\sum_j(1-a_j)\), for \(0\leq a_j\leq1\), implies that the squared Hellinger distance of the conditional predictive laws is at most the sum of these component bounds.

It remains to average over the common exact-uniform design.  Fixed local support implies that two adjacent vertices have covariates at Euclidean distance at most \(C_2h_n\).  A specified set of \(k\) indices can be connected only if one of its \(k^{k-2}\) labeled spanning trees has every edge this short.  Rooting a tree and integrating its vertices successively under the uniform density bounds this event by
\[
 k^{k-2}(C_3h_n^d)^{k-1}.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 H^2(\bar P_{0,\sigma}^{(n)},\bar P_{1,\sigma}^{(n)})
 &\leq
 \delta_n^2\sum_{k=2}^n {n\choose k}C_1^k k^{k-2}(C_3h_n^d)^{k-1}\\
 &\leq C_4n^2h_n^d\delta_n^2
 \sum_{k=2}^n(C_5nh_n^d)^{k-2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here \({n\choose k}\leq n^k/k!\) and \(k^{k-2}/k!\leq e^k\), the latter following from \(\sum_{j=1}^k\log j\geq\int_1^k\log x\,dx\).

At the selected scale,
\[
 nh_n^d\asymp
 \epsilon^{d/s_0}n^{(2s_0-d)/(2s_0+d)}.
\]
If \(d>2s_0\), this tends to zero.  If \(d=2s_0\), it is bounded by a fixed multiple of \(\epsilon^2\).  Thus, in either case, choosing \(\epsilon\) sufficiently small makes the geometric sum uniformly bounded for all sufficiently large \(n\).  We obtain
\[
 H^2(\bar P_{0,\sigma}^{(n)},\bar P_{1,\sigma}^{(n)})
 \leq C_6n^2h_n^d\delta_n^2
 \leq C_7\epsilon^{2+d/s_0}.
\]
This bound is uniform in \(\sigma\).  Squared Hellinger distance is jointly convex: pointwise Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \sqrt{\left(\int p_\sigma\,d\Pi\right)
              \left(\int q_\sigma\,d\Pi\right)}
 \geq\int\sqrt{p_\sigma q_\sigma}\,d\Pi.
\]
Integration therefore gives the same bound after averaging over the common outer-sign prior.  In particular, no additional outer-sign term remains.  Since total variation is at most the Hellinger distance under the convention used here, decreasing \(\epsilon\) once more ensures
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(\bar P_0^{(n)},\bar P_1^{(n)})
 <1-a_0-b_0=\frac34.
\]

Every component in the null mixture belongs to \(\mathcal H_0\), so a test in \(\Phi_n\) has null-mixture rejection probability at most \(a_0\).  If that test had type-II error at most \(b_0\) for every law with \(D(P)\geq c_D\delta_n\), its alternative-mixture rejection probability would be at least \(1-b_0\).  The difference of the two rejection expectations would then be at least \(1-a_0-b_0=3/4\), contradicting the total-variation bound.  Hence no such test exists and
\[
 \rho_n^*\geq c_D\epsilon n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}.
\]
The argument is an original fixed-\(n\), all-test comparison and uses only priors supported on the original class.  At \(d=2s_0\) the small fixed value of \(\epsilon\), rather than a scale union, controls the geometric series, which proves the asserted absence of a logarithm in this converse.

For the other lower term, any observational test \(\phi(O^n)\) induces the known-propensity test \((O^n,e_P)\mapsto\phi(O^n)\) with identical rejection probabilities.  Thus the definition of the two experiments gives \(\rho_{n,e}^*\leq\rho_n^*\).  The lower half of \(\texttt{lem:known-propensity-benchmark}\) yields
\[
 \rho_n^*\geq\rho_{n,e}^*\geq c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}.
\]
Combining the two inequalities proves the displayed maximum.

Finally take \(d=\gamma=1\) and \(\alpha=\beta=1/10\), so \(s_0=1/5\).  Then
\[
 \delta_n=\epsilon n^{-2/7},
 \qquad
 q_e=q_b=2\sqrt{\delta_n},
 \qquad
 h_n\asymp\delta_n^5,
 \qquad
 H_n\asymp\delta_n.
\]
Consequently
\[
 nh_n\asymp\epsilon^5n^{-3/7}\longrightarrow0,
 \qquad
 \frac{H_n}{h_n}\asymp\delta_n^{-4},
 \qquad
 H^2(\bar P_0^{(n)},\bar P_1^{(n)})\leq C\epsilon^7.
\]
The dyadic choice makes \(H_n/h_n\) an integer while preserving these comparisons, and the preceding constraint check verifies all Hölder, margin, exact-uniform-design, and componentwise constant-null requirements.  The known-propensity upper bound in \(\texttt{lem:known-propensity-benchmark}\) is \(\rho_{n,e}^*\leq Cn^{-2/5}\).  Division of the two positive bounds gives
\[
 \frac{\rho_n^*}{\rho_{n,e}^*}
 \geq c n^{2/5-2/7}=c n^{4/35},
\]
as claimed.  At the same tuple, \(t=\min\{\gamma,\alpha+\beta\}=1/5\) and \(d=1>4t\), so \(\texttt{prop:single-scale-upper}\) gives
\[
 \rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4t/(4t+3d)}=Cn^{-4/19}.
\]
This completes the stress-point bracket.
added_lemmas.justification: The common-singleton Hellinger normalization can be optimized throughout the sparse collision regime, giving an original fixed-sample nuisance converse on the unchanged causal class.
added_lemmas.gap: This lower map does not match the current all-regime upper map outside the already proved no-penalty region, and the connected-component summation does not control the dense regime where \(d<2(\alpha+\beta)\).
added_lemmas.consumer: The complete-frontier question and the downstream comparison of unknown- and known-propensity experiments.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Construct a total multiresolution test with a population signal that remains nonzero on the exact covariance-masking alternative, prove uniform finite-sample level and power including every sparse-occupancy projection, and optimize it; extend the constant-null-supported converse to the dense collision regime \(d<2(\alpha+\beta)\), then compare the independently obtained maps and determine the remaining boundary logarithms.
open_obligations.obstruction: The new lower construction controls all connected collision clusters when \(d\geq2(\alpha+\beta)\), but at its natural scale \(nh^d\to\infty\) when \(d<2(\alpha+\beta)\), so the geometric connected-component bound no longer closes.  On the upper side, \(\texttt{prop:pair-factor-omnibus-blind-alternative}\) supplies an original-class alternative with \(D(P)\asymp\delta\) and \(g_B(1/8)=0\) in every fine bin, annihilating the proposed pair-factor \(2+1\) and \(2+2\) population signals.  This is an obstruction to that architecture only; no all-test or all-statistic impossibility is claimed.
open_obligations.attempted: The sign-conditioned common one-observation marginal was used before comparing the prior predictives.  Component cell probabilities were bounded below by \(1/16\), the atom-moment discrepancy was bounded by \(\delta\), and the bounded-overlap collision graph was summed over labeled spanning trees.  This yields \(H^2\leq Cn^2h^d\delta^2\) and the sparse nuisance lower rate \(n^{-2(\alpha+\beta)/(2(\alpha+\beta)+d)}\), with no extra outer-sign term.  At the stress tuple the scale was optimized to \(n^{-2/7}\).  A richer full four-cell multinomial score was considered as the next upper route, but no uniform alternative dichotomy and complete concentration proof were obtained in this bounded round.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Let \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\), and define
\[
 b_n=
 \begin{cases}
 n^{-2\min\{\gamma,s_0\}/(4\min\{\gamma,s_0\}+d)},&d\leq4\min\{\gamma,s_0\},\\
 n^{-4\min\{\gamma,s_0\}/(4\min\{\gamma,s_0\}+3d)},&d>4\min\{\gamma,s_0\}.
 \end{cases}
\]
The proved all-regime upper bound is \(\rho_n^*\leq Cb_n\), and the known-propensity converse gives \(\rho_n^*\geq c n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)}\).  The new sparse-regime null-supported construction additionally proves, whenever \(d\geq2s_0\),
\[
 \rho_n^*\geq c\max\left\{
 n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},
 n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}
 \right\}.
\]
At \(d=2s_0\) this converse has no logarithmic loss.  If \(\gamma>s_0\) and \(d>2s_0\gamma/(\gamma-s_0)\), the nuisance term is strictly larger than the known-propensity order and certifies
\[
 \frac{\rho_n^*}{\rho_{n,e}^*}
 \geq c n^{,2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
In particular, at \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\),
\[
 c n^{-2/7}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4/19},
 \qquad
 \rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\geq c n^{4/35}.
\]
The previously proved no-penalty region \(\alpha+\beta\geq\gamma\) and \(d\leq4\gamma\) remains matched, with no logarithm at \(d=4\gamma\).  Outside these closed subregions, the lower and upper exponents do not match.  For \(d<2s_0\), the present collision expansion has \(nh_n^d\to\infty\), so connected components of unbounded order are not controlled by its geometric summation.  On the upper side, \(\texttt{prop:pair-factor-omnibus-blind-alternative}\) gives a legal alternative with \(D(P)\asymp\delta\) but zero population mean for every proposed statistic containing the specified within-bin covariance factor.  A richer full-cell signal with a uniform deterministic alternative dichotomy, all of its sparse-occupancy projections, and finite-sample calibration has not been constructed.  Thus the independently derived maps are not yet matched, transition logarithms beyond the proved boundaries remain unknown, the frozen \(r_{\mathrm{test}}\) and \(r_{\mathrm{mix}}\) remain diagnostics, and no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

prose_updates.tldr: Let \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\).  The observational critical radius now has an original fixed-sample nuisance lower bound in the sparse collision regime: if \(d\geq2s_0\), then \(\rho_n^*\geq c\max\{n^{-2\gamma/(4\gamma+d)},n^{-2s_0/(2s_0+d)}\}\), with no logarithm at \(d=2s_0\).  The existing explicit profiled fourth-order test still gives the all-regime upper rate \(b_n\), and the no-penalty region \(s_0\geq\gamma\), \(d\leq4\gamma\) remains matched.  At \((d,\gamma,\alpha,\beta)=(1,1,1/10,1/10)\), the sharper bracket is \(c n^{-2/7}\leq\rho_n^*\leq Cn^{-4/19}\), while \(\rho_n^*/\rho_{n,e}^*\geq c n^{4/35}\).  The complete upper frontier remains open because the proposed pair-factor statistics are blind to a legal covariance-masking alternative; no common sharp-rate symbol is defined.

project_justification.gap: Published CATE-homogeneity procedures and adjacent minimax results do not give the fixed-sample critical radius on this project-specific binary exact-uniform class.  The new direct-Hellinger construction determines a nuisance-driven converse throughout \(d\geq2(\alpha+\beta)\), but the best available upper map does not match it outside the established no-penalty region, and the dense collision regime remains unresolved.
project_justification.niche: The live niche is the interaction among a composite unknown-constant CATE null, separately rough propensity and baseline functions, exact full-cube design, and connected repeated-cell collisions.  A sharp result must combine a componentwise homogeneous null prior with an omnibus signal richer than binned covariance factors and must control all sparse and dense occupancy projections.
project_justification.fill: The paper now supplies the explicit total profiled fourth-order test and all-regime upper bound, the known-propensity benchmark and matched no-penalty region, and a same-class fixed-\(n\) lower construction giving \(n^{-2(\alpha+\beta)/(2(\alpha+\beta)+d)}\) whenever \(d\geq2(\alpha+\beta)\).  At the canonical rough tuple this improves the converse to \(n^{-2/7}\) and proves a polynomial cost of unknown propensity.  The covariance-masking witness precisely explains why the attempted pair-factor upper statistic does not close the remaining frontier.

prose_updates.related_work: KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024 remains a method donor rather than the source of the present class: its pointwise-estimation model is larger and its binary lower submodel uses a support with holes.  The new converse uses the localized fuzzy-hypothesis idea only after proving exact full-cube uniform masses, componentwise binary margins, a common sign-conditioned singleton predictive law, and a bounded-overlap connected-graph Hellinger calculation on this class.  NeykovBalakrishnanWasserman2021 gives collision-sensitive conditional-independence testing under a different null and metric; LundborgKimShahSamworth2024, corresponding to PCM arXiv:2211.02039, gives projected-covariance validity and spline power under common-smoothness conditions; DukesStensrudBrioschiHudson2026, arXiv:2410.00985v4, gives asymptotic structured-rule homogeneity results under nuisance conditions; and McGrathMukherjee2026, arXiv:2212.14857v5, derives separate resolutions for estimating a signed expected conditional covariance.  None supplies the componentwise constant-null, original fixed-sample nuisance lower map proved here, nor an omnibus test that overcomes the displayed covariance-masking alternative on the identical class.
prose_updates.interpretation: In sparse rough-nuisance regimes, repeated-cell scarcity creates a detectability cost that persists without positing any nuisance estimator.  At \((1,1,1/10,1/10)\), heterogeneity smaller than order \(n^{-2/7}\) cannot be uniformly detected when the propensity is unknown, whereas supplying it permits order \(n^{-2/5}\); the radius ratio therefore grows at least as \(n^{4/35}\).  This is a worst-case experiment comparison and a benchmark for workflow design, not a validation of a fitted forest or a license to interpret non-rejection as constant treatment effect.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: With \(s_0=\alpha+\beta\), the optimized lower construction takes \(h\asymp\delta^{1/s_0}\), \(H\asymp\max\{h,\delta^{1/\gamma}\}\), \(q_e=2\delta^{\alpha/s_0}\), and \(q_b=2\delta^{\beta/s_0}\).  Original margins bound every conditional binary cell probability below by \(1/16\).  Conditional on macro signs, exact singleton matching and fine-coordinate independence give a connected-component discrepancy bounded by \(C^k\delta\); exact uniform design and a spanning-tree count then give \(H^2\leq Cn^2h^d\delta^2\sum_{k\geq2}(Cnh^d)^{k-2}\).  This yields the stated rate when \(d\geq2s_0\), including the equality boundary after choosing a small fixed amplitude.  When \(d<2s_0\), \(nh^d\to\infty\) at that scale and this summation does not control high-order connected clusters.  The fixed-reference fifth projection remains a valid warning about that normalization, but it is absent after common-singleton normalization.  The upper-side obstruction is different: a legal alternative annihilates every proposed population kernel with the specified within-bin pair factor, so a full-cell alternative dichotomy and its concentration theory are still required.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The causal estimand and statistical class remain unchanged: binary outcomes, exact uniform design on the full cube, fixed overlap and interior margins, three fixed Hölder indices, and an unknown constant null.  No nuisance-rate, learner, or estimator-side condition was added.  The proved content is an all-regime bracket, a matched sufficient no-penalty region, and the new sparse-regime nuisance converse; at the rough stress tuple the remaining exponents are \(2/7\) and \(4/19\), so the frontier is not claimed sharp.  The strict known-versus-unknown region certified by the new lower bound is sufficient, not necessary.  Dense-regime lower optimization, the omnibus upper construction, and unproved transition logarithms remain open.  No result certifies an existing causal forest, and non-rejection is not evidence of homogeneity.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the field-tier target: the new sparse-regime converse must still be matched by a total uniformly calibrated omnibus test, and the dense-regime converse and transition boundaries must be completed on the identical class.
statement_notes.gap: The lower map now closes for \(d\geq2(\alpha+\beta)\), but its connected-cluster series fails at the natural scale when \(d<2(\alpha+\beta)\).  The upper pair-factor architecture is invalidated by the scoped covariance-masking alternative, and no richer full-cell statistic with a deterministic alternative dichotomy and complete occupancy concentration has yet been proved.
statement_notes.consumer: A completed theorem would give causal-forest calibration and epidemiologic heterogeneity workflows a genuine detectability benchmark and an omnibus finite-sample procedure, without certifying a fitted forest or turning non-rejection into evidence of homogeneity.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem harvests the optimized sign-conditioned common-marginal comparison and identifies a computable nuisance lower map on the unchanged class.
statement_notes.gap: It is a converse only and does not determine the dense-regime lower map or an attaining upper test.
statement_notes.consumer: It strengthens the complete-frontier bracket and certifies a strict value of known propensity on an explicit rough parameter region.
